posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

They invaded and devastated farmers' wheat fields and the government had no other option but to take out the big guns, literally. What followed has since become one of the strangest military operations in the history: the Great Emu War.

On the vast, cold seas with endless waves in all directions, there is one constant companion: the stars. Whenever they were visible, sailors knew they could find their way. Their guidance meant ships could dare to cross the oceans with nothing more than keen eyesight and the ability to read the signs in the sky. Just like the brave sailors aboard Chinese junks that can be seen on the July page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, who left familiar shores to cross oceans and head into the unknown.

Imagine stepping inside a cathedral carved entirely from salt… ⁠
@simran_joy_ has officially made us crave this one-of-a-kind sightseeing experience.

The Manta Resort’s Underwater Room, located near Pemba Island in Tanzania, is a floating three-level retreat with a bedroom 4 meters below the surface of the Indian Ocean. ⁠
⁠
Through the underwater windows, guests can watch tropical fish swim by during the day and see marine life gather around the lights at night.⁠
⁠
Above the water, there’s a private deck for relaxing and taking in the views, but the real experience happens below the surface, where the ocean becomes your view, your soundtrack,

Guatemala is home to one of the world's most unique dining experiences. ⁠
At @pizzapacayadedavid visitors can enjoy freshly cooked pizza using the volcano's natural heat while taking in spectacular views.⁠
Thanks @agorgeousangel for sharing this incredible adventure!

It may look like the entrance to a fantasy world, but this incredible monument is real.⁠
⁠
The Chronicle of Georgia stands high above Tbilisi with 16 towering pillars carved with scenes from the country's history and Christianity. Rising to 35 meters (115 feet) tall, it's one of the most impressive monuments in the Caucasus.⁠
⁠
Despite its enormous size, it remains one of Georgia's lesser-known attractions, making it feel even more mysterious.⁠
⁠
From its hilltop location, you'll also get breath
@malakai.barcly takes us on one of the most unforgettable kayaking adventure… and yes, it involves seals!

These unusual bamboo boats have been part of Vietnam’s coastline for centuries.⁠
⁠
They’re known as Thúng Chai, or “basket boats,” and they were created by local fishermen and became a clever solution during the French colonial era, when traditional boats were taxed.⁠
⁠
Today, they are still used by fishing communities across central Vietnam, and their unique design even allows them to serve as emergency boats during storms and floods.⁠
⁠
Visitors can also experience a ride in one around Hoi An,

Adrenaline junkies, this one's calling your name!⁠
Ice karting in Lapland, Finland is officially a new bucket-list adventure.⁠
⁠
🎥: @ya3gobz

Built into the side of a mountain in northern Italy, Madonna della Corona is a church unlike most others.⁠
⁠
Located near Verona, the sanctuary sits 774 meters above sea level and was built into the cliffs of Monte Baldo.⁠
⁠
The first chapel appeared here centuries ago, and today the site remains an important pilgrimage destination.⁠
⁠
By: Julien R

Ever seen bus stops shaped like giant fruits? 🍓🍉🍊⁠
⁠
Along Route 207 in Konagai, Isahaya, Japan, you’ll find 16 colorful fruit-shaped bus stops originally created for the Journey Exposition Nagasaki 1990. Their popularity made them a permanent attraction.⁠
⁠
@thetrekkinbird showed us this unique roadside gem featuring five fruit designs: strawberry, watermelon, melon, mikan, and tomato. 🍅✨⁠
Would you go hunting for them all?

The Andes are home to millions of Quechua people who have spent generations adapting to life in the mountains.⁠
⁠
Their traditions are woven into everyday life, from the food they grow and the clothes they make to the animals they care for and the knowledge passed down through their communities.⁠
⁠
Even today, many Quechua communities continue to preserve a way of life that has lasted for centuries.⁠
⁠
By: Gustavo Leighton

The magic of a European summer. ⁠
Delicious cocktails delivered atop a 500-year-old tower it doesn't get much more iconic than that.⁠
⁠
Thanks, @itsbellaceto, for sharing this first-class cocktail experience!

Most people visit Table Mountain for the views, but if you're lucky, you'll catch something even more memorable. ☁️⁠
⁠
When the weather is just right, clouds roll over the mountain's flat summit and spill down the sides, creating what's known as the "tablecloth."⁠
⁠
The effect can last for hours or disappear almost as quickly as it arrived, which is why no two visits look exactly the same.⁠
⁠
By: @ryanlans @brigittepegado @tomas_wells @magda_ehlers_photography @arthurbrognoli op23

This video is a rare sighting of an elusive, so-called “ghost population” of great whites that call the temperate and busy waters of the Mediterranean home. Can you find the gecko?

Photographer @chienleephotography photographed this mossy leaf-tailed gecko (Uroplatus sikorae) hiding in plain sight in Mantadia National Park, Madagascar. These geckos have uncanny camouflaging abilities, which are needed in a rainforest filled with keen-eyed predators. When resting, they face downward to catch unsuspecting insects climbing from the ground and to prevent their eyes from reflecting light that can alert birds to their presence.

Have you ever seen an orca ram a sunfish so hard that it was smashed to bits? This incredible footage of one orca holding the fish by the tail while another rammed it was captured by marine biologist and National Geographic Explorer Katy Ayres, and it raises several questions about the purpose of this behavior. Sunfish are the heaviest bony fish on the planet, but an orca can easily kill them, leading some researchers to theorize it may be a game rather than a hunting tactic.

Retiring at 100 years old? Not a chance! Here’s a sneak peek of Sir David Attenborough working on the narration for the upcoming BLUE PLANET III.

#DavidAttenborough100 #DavidAttenborough #BluePlanetIII

Nature never fails to surprise us 🌍

Discover 20 unforgettable Planet Earth moments that prove the natural world is stranger, smarter and more spectacular than we can ever imagine. 

Head over to the link in our bio to read the full article 🔗

#PlanetEarth #ExtraordinaryAnimals #PE20

Is the anus an underrated innovation? 🍑

Mutations in an ancestor called the urbilaterian lengthened their bodies over generations. A tube formed with a mouth for eating and an anus for pooing. This was a breakthrough invention creating the one-way through-gut for continuous feeding.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

A mouthful of teeth 🦁🦷

30 to be precise. As predators and carnivores, lions use their teeth to hunt and eat. They have twelve incisors, four canines, ten premolars and four molars for gripping prey and cutting meat.

#EarthCapture by @jackswynnerton
.
.
.
.
#Lion #Wildlife #Nature

Waiting for the perfect moment 🐆
 
Perched high above the ground, the leopard waits until an impala comes within striking distance. After staying completely still, it launches from the tree in one powerful leap, but will all that patience pay off?
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

How do you attract a female? 🦌🦕

The most attractive are usually the biggest and hairiest with prominent features. In reproduction, they pass their genes to the next generation, who inherit more exaggerated attributes. Over millions of years, animal traits modify for better mating chances.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Someone’s got serious aim 🎯
 
An archerfish doesn’t chase its prey. Instead, it fires a powerful jet of water with remarkable precision, knocking unsuspecting insects straight into the water. One perfectly placed shot is all it takes before the fish darts in to claim its meal. 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Penises come in all shapes and sizes 🍆

Shells prevented reptiles from fertilising their eggs, yet evolution created a solution: the penis. Reptiles were among the first animals to have them, but they weren’t the last. For life on land, it meant sex as we know it had been invented.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

🦦 Otter vs otter 🦦

Despite their cute reputation, fierce otter fights aren’t uncommon. Clashes over territories, food supplies and mating disputes can break out and become intense. Some end in serious injury, or even death.

EarthCapture by @jbucketslist
.
.
.
.
#Otters #Wildlife #Nature

It’s World Chimpanzee Day 🐵

Chimps share DNA with humans, but Dr Jane Goodall discovered other similarities making them our closest living relatives. They use tools, hold hands, embrace one another and use non-verbal communication like humans too. 

#EarthCapture via Shutterstock 📸

1. Patrick Rolands
2. Cheryl Ramalho
3. Nadine Wagner
4. Andrew Lilley
5. Gudkov Andrey

#WorldChimpanzeeDay #JaneGoodall #Nature

Warthog snouts are survival tools 🐗

It’s used for sniffing, digging and foraging, but they must bend their legs to reach the ground. Another creature evolved a longer snout for the same purpose, and it developed a body shape we recognise today.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature
